extracted.intended_audience: general readers, journalists, and policymakers interested in Czech government policy on disinformation
extracted.subtask_description: Summary of the Czech government's 2022 Action Plan against Disinformation prepared by Michal Klíma, outlining proposed definitions, institutional measures, legal responses, and funding for organizations and media to counter disinformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of disinformation
rubrics_metrics.description: "online content that threatens the sovereignty, territorial integrity, democratic foundations or internal order and security of the Czech Republic" (definition given in the draft)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the draft strategy's working definition as reported in the leaked draft available to Echo24 editors; frames disinformation in terms of national security and democratic stability rather than mere falsehoods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blocking disinformation (site shutdowns)
rubrics_metrics.description: Possible ways of blocking disinformation, including shutting down websites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The strategy proposes blocking disinformation and notes precedents where some sites were shut down following the Russian invasion of Ukraine, often with no legislative backing — implying a need for legal frameworks to authorize blocking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctioning publishers
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The draft lists sanctioning publishers as a tool alongside blocking and prosecution; presented as part of a menu of enforcement measures to deter dissemination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prosecuting authors and distributors
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposes prosecuting authors and distributors of disinformation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The plan envisages criminal or other legal action against those who create or distribute disinformation that meets the draft's threat criteria; presented together with sanctions and blocking as enforcement options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial support for non-profit organisations combating disinformation
rubrics_metrics.description: State support for non-profit organisations that deal with disinformation with 50 million Kč per year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The draft proposes an annual allocation to non-profits working on disinformation — a proactive, funded civil-society approach to countering disinformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: State funding for 'friendly' or 'correct' media
rubrics_metrics.description: Give 100 million Kč per year from the state budget to friendly media that would help the state in the fight against disinformation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The draft recommends budgetary transfers to media deemed to assist the state; this proposal attracted controversy (e.g., government distancing and opposition from publishers) due to implications for media independence and state influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creation of a national coordinator against disinformation
rubrics_metrics.description: Envisaged creation of the position of a national coordinator against disinformation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The draft proposes a central coordinating post; historically the government later abolished the government commissioner role and transferred the agenda to the national security advisor, reflecting administrative choices about where the function sits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of a department against hybrid threats and terrorism
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuation/follow-up of earlier steps such as establishing a department against hybrid threats and terrorism at the Ministry of the Interior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The action plan is presented as following processes already begun (e.g., ministry-level departments and other documents addressing hybrid threats), indicating institutionalizing counter-disinformation within security structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat draft as a working proposal pending government discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: The government characterized the document as only a working proposal that had not yet been discussed by the Cabinet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operationally, proposals in the draft require formal government discussion and approval before implementation; media reporting of leaked drafts does not equate to governmental adoption.
